title: detect records changed_utc in _fetch_state.csv, so a pack's [source changed] mark can fire on the live kb
goal: Retrospective of SP-tm4wlsve: ST-ebn65qen's [source changed] mark compares an anchor's verified_utc with its source's _fetch_state.csv changed_utc, but no row of the kb's _fetch_state.csv files holds a changed_utc (0 of 2590 rows on 2026-10-12), so the mark never fires on the live kb and its check passed only on planted state. factdiff detect writes changed_utc when it finds a source changed (or the stamp reads the change date from the field detect does write), and a test runs detect on a planted changed page and finds the date in the state row and the mark on a pack line citing it.
notes: Merged from BG-w3p7fqy2 “factdiff.py detect never records changed_utc, so no source of _fetch_state.csv has a recorded change” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: Its own note names ST-fxz2wrfe as the duplicate; its repro now passes spuriously (85 kb/public rows hold changed_utc, written by fetch.py on first fetch) while factdiff.py still has no changed_utc write. Its goal: factdiff.py detect writes the state row's changed_utc when a source's verdict is changed, replaced or moved, so the change history in git and the source changed mark of a fact read it; the repro exits 0 once a detect run has recorded a change. Its repro: {"run": ["python3", "-c", "import csv, sys; sys.exit(0 if any(r['changed_utc'] for r in csv.DictReader(open('kb/public/_fetch_state.csv', encoding='utf-8'))) else 1)"]}
